page: Microsoft Azure FX64-16mds_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the FXmdsv2 family. It is configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system features a massive memory allocation of 1344.0 GB, yielding 84.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 3780 GB, and the instance is premium storage capable. No GPUs are present on this virtual machine, which runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2353.0 and a text processing score of 2923.0, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is strong at 91.75 GB/sec, and single-threaded gzip compression reaches 34.06 GB/sec. Multi-core performance, such as the stress-ng multi-core score of 17738.0 and Geekbench multi-core score of 13593.0, falls within the average range. LLM inference for text generation using a small 135M model is strong at 327.43 tokens/sec, while larger model processing remains average.

The server exhibits a high resource density of memory relative to compute cores, making it a specialized option where memory capacity is prioritized over high parallel core counts. This qualitative profile offers cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive multi-threaded CPU scaling. Appropriate workloads include large-scale in-memory databases, memory-intensive enterprise applications, caching layers, and single-threaded data processing tasks that benefit from the high 4.2 GHz clock speed and extensive RAM.
description: Microsoft Azure FX64-16mds_v2 is a memory-optimized x86_64 server from the FXmdsv2 family, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs from an 8-core Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, paired with an extensive 1344.0 GB of RAM and 3780 GB of local storage. The server delivers top-tier single-core performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2353.0 and strong large-block memory write bandwidth of 91.75 GB/sec. While multi-core benchmarks and database operations sit in the average tier, its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 84.0 GB per core provides specialized efficiency for memory-intensive applications. This hardware profile is best suited for large in-memory databases, heavy caching layers, and single-threaded data processing workloads requiring massive memory capacity without excessive parallel CPU scaling.
